rounds.fact: Tucows started in 1993 as a curated shareware download library (the name stood for 'The Ultimate Collection of Winsock Software') before evolving into an internet services company.
Twitter launched in 2006 and the 140-character limit came directly from SMS constraints, since early tweets were literally sent and received as text messages.
Nintendo's site in the early 2000s was promoting both the GameCube and Game Boy Advance simultaneously, an unusually broad two-console push even by Nintendo's standards.
Dogpile was a 'metasearch' engine that combined results from multiple search engines at once, a workaround from an era when no single search engine indexed the whole web well.
The Drudge Report has used essentially the same barebones, all-links homepage design since the late 90s, a deliberate choice that's stayed almost untouched for over two decades.
